findings.what: The words present 58.9 Hz, the frequency 0.1 s after the step, as the frequency dip and then say the governor adds fuel and the speed climbs back, but the speed keeps falling until the fuel has caught up with the load: the rule bottoms out at about 57.1 Hz at 0.38 s, and the trace on screen 4 shows 58.0 Hz with the fuel at only 4%, so add one sentence that the fall goes on until the engine's torque matches the load's again and that 58.9 Hz is only where it has got to by 0.1 s.

Screen 7 leaves the set isochronous at 60 Hz, but screen 8 opens isochronous at 62.4 Hz and 1872 rev/min with no word why, and 'So no load sits at 62.4 Hz and full load at 60 Hz' only follows if the set point was chosen to give 60 Hz on full load; say that in one sentence, as the explain text does.

The explain carries five footnotes, and three of them sit on sentences that are not a rule or value Dan would look up ('This fall is a frequency dip', 'The governor and the AVR are the two basic controls on every set', 'speed control is what shares the kW'); keep the droop definition's [^2] and [^3] and drop the rest.

'A governor tuned too eagerly overshoots and swings about its speed' gives hunting a cause that no source in sources or quotes.json supports, and the brief's gaps say to quote one before saying more than the name; either cite a quote or cut it to naming the swing.

findings.where: Screen 10 (The set point), text and read
findings.what: 'Then the dot settles at the top of its line, 62.4 Hz' is only true if Dan leaves the set point at 62.4 Hz; if he drags it to 63.0 Hz and then taps Trip it settles at 63.0 Hz, so say 'at the top of its line, its set point'.

findings.where: Screen 12 (Fault or design?), the right choice
findings.what: 'Design: droop working, with the set point too low' calls a 57.6 Hz full-load frequency 'design' in the same breath as a wrong setting; 'No fault: droop working as set, but the set point needs raising' says the same thing without the mixed message.

No screen says what droop is for; the explain's 'speed control is what shares the kW' does not say that droop is what lets sets share, so one sentence on screen 10 ('Its use shows when two sets share one load') would answer 'why would anyone choose it?'.

findings.where: Set picture, the two torque arrows
findings.what: The torques are drawn as straight arrows along the shaft, which read as an axial push and pull; curved arrows round the shaft, or a short label 'turning effort', would show a torque honestly.

findings.where: Screen 10, the droop graph during the trip
findings.what: A trip from 252 kW peaks at about 66.8 Hz, above the graph's 66 Hz top, so the dot pins against the top edge for a moment while the tile reads 66.6 Hz; raise the axis to 68 Hz or say nothing is lost there.
The caption about a strobe and the flywheel's mark shows under the two screens that have no picture; hide it there, and 'slowed three times' reads better as 'shown three times slower than real'.

The first picture is entirely still (steady 60 Hz, the strobe holding the mark, no demo), so the interactive opens without anything moving; a short demonstration that briefly unbalances and rebalances the two arrows would make it look alive.

'To run at a chosen frequency at a chosen load, set the no-load set point to that frequency + the droop in hertz × the load ÷ the rated load' runs to 30 words; split it into the fall at that load, then add it to the chosen frequency.
